transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Start: 15:00 UTC / 11:00 ET
Duration: 52 minutes (recording truncated at 52:01)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Patel (Redwood SE), Rajat Singh (StratusGrid - Lead ML Eng), Lena Ortiz (StratusGrid - Platform), Samir Qureshi (StratusGrid - CTO)

Summary:
- Quick readout of this week's benchmark run (48h rolling windows) comparing Redwood POC vs incumbent baseline vendor.
- Focus on latency (p50/p95/p99) and sustained throughput (rps) plus tail behavior during spikes.
- Routing/placement handoff discussion for moving from hosted pilot to a dedicated slot behind StratusGrid VPC.
- Action items: share logs, provision dedicated trial, confirm security checklist and soak test start date.

Topics:
- Bench numbers vs baseline (p50/p95/p99)
- Throughput and cold/warm start behavior
- KV cache and batching config changes applied this sprint
- Dedicated slot sizing and VPC peering checklist
- Security artifacts (SOC2, KMS, audit logs) and SSO integration

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for carving the time, we'll run quick through the results then talk routing handoff.
[00:12] Rajat Singh: cool, we've got Samir and I—Lena joined—so yeah looking forward.
[00:18] Ethan Patel: great. quick note before we jump in, the numbers are from the 48‑hour sweep we ran Mon‑Wed, all traces and raw logs are in the sheet we linked in chat. some of the samples include heavy prompt lengths (~512 tokens) and mixture of few‑shot calls.
[00:34] Lena Ortiz: and we specifically care about p95 under 1s for our main endpoint, that's the bar our UX team set.
[00:40] Maya Chen: understood. ok Ethan, take it away on the topline.
[00:44] Ethan Patel: sure. so top line: Redwood POC — p50 120ms, p95 780ms, p99 1.45s under steady load at 180 rps; baseline vendor — p50 210ms, p95 1.25s, p99 2.1s at ~130 rps. throughput wise we sustained 220 rps peak short bursts with batching tweaks, sustained plateau around 180 rps. note — those numbers are for our recommended quantized model variant and with KV prefix caching enabled for repeated prompts.
[01:16] Rajat Singh: wait p50 120ms seems low, are we measuring token step or end‑to‑end request?
[01:22] Ethan Patel: good call — these are end‑to‑end wall clock latencies for a full generate call, so includes network and model decode time, not per‑token stepping. some of the lower p50s are from cached KV hits.
[01:33] Samir Qureshi: so on average you're about 35‑40% faster p95 vs incumbent, and throughput is like X1.6, right?
[01:41] Ethan Patel: yep, roughly. the biggest wins came from continuous batching improvements and reduced kernel overhead for attention on the 40GB cards we used.
[01:49] Lena Ortiz: where did you host the workloads for this run? cloud region and VPC?
[01:53] Ethan Patel: hosted POC in us‑west2, Redwood managed cluster but isolated per‑customer namespace. for the dedicated trial we'll spin up in your VPC via peering.
[02:03] Rajat Singh: we saw a handful of spikes around 02:14 UTC where p99 jumped to 3.1s — what's that from?
[02:10] Ethan Patel: I dug into that — two correlated factors: a) a brief model reload during a rolling kernel swap; b) a small upstream network flapping event in the peering window. we've since applied warm preloads and adjusted rolling update window to avoid that.
[02:25] Maya Chen: i'll note that in the follow ups – we flagged patches and they'll be in the runbook.

[02:30] Speaker 1: (inaudible) the warmup patch helps a lot, we saw tail drop after applying it.
[02:36] Rajat Singh: good, can you quantify?
[02:38] Ethan Patel: after warm preload p99 max during spike windows dropped from 3.1s to 1.6s in the next sweep. so still some tail but within our target for the pilot.
[02:48] Lena Ortiz: how much of this relies on the KV cache? if our workload doesn't get repeat prefixes we could lose that win.
[02:55] Ethan Patel: yep if cache hit rate drops throughput and p50 shift upward. these tests included a 35% prefix reuse rate—your production profile said 25‑30% so expect slightly higher p95s in worst case. we're provisioning a follow up run with synthetic low‑cache to show the delta.
[03:12] Maya Chen: on cost — did you compute tokens/sec or cost per 1k reqs compared to baseline?
[03:18] Ethan Patel: rough economics: cost per 1k requests normalized — Redwood pilot cost was ~0.82x the incumbent because of better utilization; main reason is 1) smarter batching and 2) quantized kernels reducing memory traffic. we'll send line‑item in the spreadsheet.
[03:31] Samir Qureshi: security — we need SOC2 and KMS flow for key material. can you confirm you support customer‑managed keys and logs?
[03:38] Maya Chen: yes — Redwood Private supports customer keys via KMS and HSM integrations; audit logs and per‑request metadata retention is configurable. Ethan will share the security pack.
[03:47] Ethan Patel: copied — the pack contains SOC2 cert, our pen test summary, KMS integration guide and audit log retention options. note for VPC/on‑prem we hand off a private control plane and you manage the peering.
[03:59] Lena Ortiz: SSO? we need SAML + SCIM provisioning for our internal teams.
[04:04] Maya Chen: supported. we'll include our SSO guide and a sample assertion mapping for your IdP.

[04:12] Rajat Singh: routing/hand off — what does the dedicated slot look like for our expected peak of 250 rps?
[04:18] Ethan Patel: for 250 sustained rps we recommend 4x 80GB‑class GPUs with a small headroom for burst (or equivalent fractional GPUs in Redwood Dedicated). for initial trial we can provision 2x A10g equiv plus burst to validate; afterwards bump to 4 for soak.
[04:31] Samir Qureshi: do you do autoscaling within Dedicated or is it manual?
[04:35] Ethan Patel: dedicated pools support autoscale policies, but for the enterprise pilot we usually run manual scale steps to avoid noisy neighbours during evaluation. you'll have control over thresholds.

[04:44] Lena Ortiz: paperwork question — will the dedicated trial be under our account so we can run billing/usage auditing?
[04:50] Maya Chen: yes, we can enable billing visibility and token‑level usage reports. for the pilot we typically provide pilot credits and exportable CSVs.

[05:00] Rajat Singh: on integration friction — network team asked about NAT egress and how we handle private images.
[05:06] Ethan Patel: for private deployments we can accept customer‑provided images or run within your private registry; egress is controlled by you via peering, no internet egress if you prefer.

[05:14] Speaker 2: (unclear) latency during cold starts — how long to warm?
[05:18] Ethan Patel: cold start on a full model reload is ~18–25s, but with continuous warmers we keep warm instances and that drops to sub‑2s for request‑level warm‑up.

[05:27] Maya Chen: ok, next let's run through the specific bench diffs in the sheet, page 2. Ethan?
[05:31] Ethan Patel: page 2 — breakdown by prompt length. small prompts (<64 tokens): p95 about 420ms (Redwood) vs 680ms baseline. medium prompts (64‑256): p95 610ms vs 1.05s baseline. large prompts (256‑512): p95 1.05s vs 1.8s baseline. throughput concurrency curves show Redwood maintaining lower latency at higher QPS due to dynamic batching and prefix cache heuristics.
[06:02] Rajat Singh: metrics look promising. is there anything in the run that overestimates Redwood? e.g., synthetic latency artifacts?
[06:09] Ethan Patel: we tried to mirror your traces; Rajat you shared representative traces and we replayed them. there is always some replay bias, but we also ran randomized traces that lowered the cache hit rate to 10% to stress worst‑case; even there Redwood p95 was ~1.3s vs baseline 1.9s.
[06:25] Lena Ortiz: about the randomized low‑cache test — did that use larger batch windows? batch size configs?
[06:30] Ethan Patel: for low‑cache test we constrained batch window to 15ms and used a max batch size of 32; default test had 40ms window and max 64. we can tune down if you want lower tail variance.

[06:42] Samir Qureshi: ok. what does the handoff flow look like — we want to move to a VPC peered dedicated slot and then cut over traffic in stages.
[06:49] Maya Chen: we recommend a 3‑phase handoff: 1) provision dedicated slot + smoke tests in your VPC; 2) 48h soak with a traffic mirror at 10% then 50%; 3) staged cutover + rollback window. Ethan will own the provisioning and runbook.
[07:05] Ethan Patel: yep i'll supply an infra runbook with IPs, healthchecks, rollback steps and metrics to watch (p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU util, queue depth).

[07:15] Rajat Singh: quick question on model versions — we need pinned versions for reproducibility. how do you handle rollouts?
[07:21] Ethan Patel: you can pin model versions per route; rollouts support canary and A/B with automatic fallback if latency or error SLOs breach.
[07:27] Lena Ortiz: do you store model weights in our S3 or your registry?
[07:31] Ethan Patel: in private deployments you can host weights in your S3 and we load from there; in hosted POC we cached weights in Redwood storage but we can change for the dedicated trial.

[07:40] Speaker 3: (background) quick note — competitor performance we've seen is inconsistent on long‑context loads, glad you're stable.
[07:46] Maya Chen: thanks — we do a bunch of long context tests too, but for this pilot the 512 token window was the primary gating.

[07:53] Rajat Singh: can you share the raw logs for the spike windows? we'll run them through our analyzer.
[07:58] Ethan Patel: yes the dropbox link in chat has the raw spans, JFR style traces, and sampling profiler output.

[08:06] Lena Ortiz: about SSO mapping — we need a sample assertion for Okta to map roles to route access.
[08:12] Maya Chen: we'll include the Okta mapping example in the SSO doc pack.

[08:18] Samir Qureshi: pricing — what can you offer for the pilot period? we need a capped spend and a view of reserved capacity pricing if we go production.
[08:25] Maya Chen: for pilots we typically provide a pilot credit pool and a short term reserved price quote for dedicated. i'll send both a capped pilot spend agreement and a 90‑day reserved price on Monday.

[08:37] Rajat Singh: last engineering nit — how do you surface per‑request metadata for downstream auditing?
[08:42] Ethan Patel: per‑request headers are stamped in audit logs and exposed in the console and via API. retention is configurable, and we support exporting logs to your S3.

[08:52] Maya Chen: ok we're at 40 minutes, let's confirm the action owners and dates.
[08:57] Ethan Patel: action list: provisioning dedicated trial by 8/22, bench artifacts by 8/21, low‑cache stress run scheduled once we get traces.

[09:07] Rajat Singh: we'll try to share an extra day of traces for weekend patterns — I'll drop them by Friday.

[09:12] Lena Ortiz: one more ask—can you include GPU util heatmaps in the next drop? that helps sizing decisions.

[09:17] Ethan Patel: yes — perf profiler heatmaps included.

[09:20] Maya Chen: perfect. recap of next steps: we send bench sheet + security pack, Ethan provisions trial in VPC, StratusGrid runs 48h soak starting 8/24, Maya will follow up on pricing.

[09:34] Samir Qureshi: good meeting. thanks team.

[09:36] Maya Chen: thanks all. we'll follow up in email and update the CRM.

End of transcript.
